KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · 35 CARDS · AGES 3–8

How to play every game in the deck.

Thirty-five classic children’s games, one short page each: the rules card itself, the three steps printed on it, what you need, and one fresh way to play it tonight. Duck Duck Goose, Hopscotch, Simon Says, Tag, Treasure Hunt and thirty more — the answers to “how do you play that?”, all in one place.

Pick a game ↓Cover first, then every rule card in file order.
HOW THE RULES PAGES WORK

The card is the rules. The page is the grown-up’s quiet answer.

Every rule card in the Kids Games deck does the same three things: names the game, shows children playing it, and prints a HOW TO PLAY panel with three numbered steps and a skill the game quietly practices — Imagine + Move, Stop + Go, Watch + Remember. Each page below shows the card first, quotes its three steps word for word, and adds what the card cannot fit: what to gather before you start, one safety-and-sanity note for grown-ups, and a fresh twist for tomorrow.

These rules pages belong to the school’s Kids Games extra class, where every card also opens a full how-to-play guide written for a kid to follow. The two shelves sit side by side: come here for the rules of a game you are about to play, and visit the class when you want the whole game afternoon laid out in tour order. If your child is working on Sports, Movement & Play — Class 37, these games are its playground cousins.

WHERE THIS SHELF FITS

Two shelves, one game cupboard.

The Kids Games extra class walks the older twenty-six-card deck in tour order — throwing games first, then chasing, table, quiet and acting games, and the sidewalk classics at the end — with a lesson a kid can follow on every page. This shelf adds the newer rule cards beside them, one short rules page per game. And for the classes already on the Learning Path, Class 37 · Sports, Movement & Play teaches forty named sports skills, step by step — these games are what the whole family plays between lessons.

Rules bend at your house. Every version here is the friendly starter version — change the words, shorten the course and stop while it is still fun.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Animal Walks.

To play Animal Walks, pick an animal and cross the room the way that animal would — bear-crawl, hop like a bunny, or waddle like a penguin — then let the next player choose a new animal.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Choose an animal movement.
  2. Move across the space like that animal.
  3. Change animals and let everyone have a turn.

Skill practiced: Imagine + Move — printed on the card.

What you need

Clear floor space and a little imagination; no equipment at all.

For grown-ups

Join in yourself: children walk braver animals when a grown-up flops down and crawls beside them. Watch for slippery socks on smooth floors.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Call out two animals at once — "crab meets flamingo" — and let your child invent the mash-up walk.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Balloon Volleyball.

Balloon Volleyball turns a piece of string into a net: tap the balloon over the line, and keep it flying on your side so it never touches the ground.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Make a low line across the play area.
  2. Tap the balloon over the line.
  3. Keep the balloon from touching the ground on your side.

Skill practiced: Tap + Cooperate — printed on the card.

What you need

A balloon and a low line — a string between two chairs or a strip of painter’s tape.

For grown-ups

Keep the line low enough that a two-year-old’s tap clears it, and let points go uncounted if counting makes someone cross — the rally is the fun.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Play sitting on the floor for a wobbly, giggly version, or make the line "water" that the balloon must not splash into.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Beanbag Balance.

In Beanbag Balance you rest a small beanbag on your head or shoulder and walk a slow, careful line from one spot to another without letting it slip.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Place a beanbag on your head or shoulder.
  2. Walk slowly from one spot to another.
  3. If it falls, pick it up and try again.

Skill practiced: Balance + Patience — printed on the card.

What you need

A beanbag — or a sock filled with rice, tied shut.

For grown-ups

Slow is the whole trick: children discover that tiny steps and steady eyes keep the bag up longer than hurrying. A soft carpet saves noisy drops.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Walk a tape line on the floor, or balance the bag while walking backwards and sideways like a tiny tightrope star.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Beanbag Relay.

Beanbag Relay is a team carry-and-run: dash to a marker with your beanbag, run it back, and pass it to the next teammate so everyone gets a turn.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Split into small teams.
  2. Carry a soft beanbag to the marker and back.
  3. Pass it to the next player until everyone has a turn.

Skill practiced: Carry + Share — printed on the card.

What you need

One soft beanbag per team and a marker — a shoe, a cone or a chair.

For grown-ups

Keep teams small and courses short so waiting never gets long, and let the smallest child run the shortest leg with the loudest cheer.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Carry the bag on a spoon, under an arm, or balanced on an open palm — a different silly carry for every lap.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Bubble Chase.

Bubble Chase is exactly what it sounds like: blow a cloud of bubbles into the air, then chase them down and pop them with gentle claps.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Blow bubbles in an open space.
  2. Chase and gently pop the bubbles.
  3. Take turns blowing and chasing.

Skill practiced: Chase + Share — printed on the card.

What you need

Bubble mix and a wand, outdoors or in a room with space to run.

For grown-ups

Take turns being the blower so nobody pops everything at once, and keep the game away from slick patios — chasing eyes do not watch feet.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Give each round a rule: only red bubbles, only the highest bubble, or pop with a shoulder, an elbow or a nose.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Colour Hunt.

To play Colour Hunt, choose three colours, then search the room or the yard together until each colour is spotted and proudly pointed at.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Choose three colours to find.
  2. Search the play area with a grown-up.
  3. Point to each colour when you spot it.

Skill practiced: Look + Match — printed on the card.

What you need

Nothing but eyes and agreed-on colours; colour cards make it feel official.

For grown-ups

A grown-up joins the hunt rather than judging it — the pointing, naming and counting along the way is the learning, so there are no winners needed.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Narrow the world: hunt only in the kitchen, only for soft things, or find both a big thing and a tiny thing in the same colour.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Duck Walk Relay.

Duck Walk Relay sends teams waddling: sink into a squat, waddle out to the marker and back, then tag the next duckling waiting in line.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Split into small teams.
  2. Waddle to the marker and back.
  3. Tag the next player and keep going until everyone has a turn.

Skill practiced: Waddle + Teamwork — printed on the card.

What you need

A marker to waddle around and legs ready to giggle.

For grown-ups

Deep squats are hard work for little legs — keep the course short and let hands rest on knees. The waddle gets funnier the slower it goes.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Race with arms tucked behind backs like real wings, or waddle while quacking a counting chant — one quack per step.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Four Square.

Four Square draws four chalk squares on the ground, one player per square, and the ball must bounce through them one square at a time without going out.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Mark four equal squares on the ground.
  2. One player stands in each square.
  3. Bounce the ball into another square and keep it moving.

Skill practiced: Bounce + Cooperate — printed on the card.

What you need

Chalk, a playground ball and four players.

For grown-ups

Let beginners get a gentle bounce in their square before real rallies start, and agree that a missed catch simply passes the serve on — no outs for the smallest players.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Name the squares A, B, C and D and call the letter before each bounce, or shrink the court so everyone takes tiny, careful bounces.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Hula Hoop Pass.

Hula Hoop Pass joins hands in a circle with one mission: pass the hoop all the way around without anyone letting go — bodies wiggle through it, not hands.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Stand in a circle and hold hands.
  2. Pass a hula hoop around the circle without letting go.
  3. Keep working together until it reaches everyone.

Skill practiced: Cooperate + Move — printed on the card.

What you need

One hula hoop and a circle of players holding hands.

For grown-ups

Start by showing the step-through move yourself — one leg, then the head, then wriggle. Cheering every hand-off keeps the circle patient.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Add two hoops travelling opposite ways, or time the circle and see if the whole team can beat its own record.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Lava Floor.

Lava Floor turns the carpet into molten danger: scatter safe stepping spots around the room, then cross the whole space without a single toe touching the lava.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Place safe stepping spots across the play area.
  2. Imagine the floor is lava.
  3. Move from spot to spot without touching the floor.

Skill practiced: Plan + Balance — printed on the card.

What you need

Cushions, paper sheets or mats for the stepping spots.

For grown-ups

Lay the spots close enough for real jumps and slide nothing that slips — rugs on hard floors can skid. Melted players simply restart, laughing.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Pretend certain spots are crocodiles or ice that cracks, or call out colours so only the named spots are safe this round.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Memory Moves.

Memory Moves is a copying game for sharp eyes: one player invents a short movement pattern — clap, jump, turn — and everyone tries to repeat it in the exact order.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. One player makes a short movement sequence.
  2. Everyone watches carefully.
  3. Try to repeat the sequence in the same order.

Skill practiced: Watch + Remember — printed on the card.

What you need

Space for one jump and any three simple moves.

For grown-ups

Start with two moves and grow by one each round; watching quietly before repeating is the real skill, so give everyone a thinking pause.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Let the pattern tell a story — "wake up, brush teeth, jump out the door" — and see who remembers the whole morning in moves.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Mirror Moves.

In Mirror Moves, partners face each other and one moves in slow motion — arm waves, face pulls, gentle steps — while the other copies everything like a reflection, then they swap.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Pair up with a partner.
  2. One player makes slow movements.
  3. The other player copies like a mirror, then swap roles.

Skill practiced: Copy + Connect — printed on the card.

What you need

A partner and a bit of standing room.

For grown-ups

Slow really is the secret: fast moves break the mirror. Take the first turn yourself and make one move very silly to check they are watching.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Pretend one of you is the reflection in a shop window, or switch leader without a signal and see how long the mirror flows on.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Musical Statues.

Musical Statues is the freeze dance: everyone dances while the music plays, and when it pauses, whoever holds perfectly still like a statue stays in the round.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Play music while everyone dances.
  2. Pause the music.
  3. Freeze like a statue; anyone who moves sits out for one round.

Skill practiced: Rhythm + Self-Control — printed on the card.

What you need

Music you can pause, and a little dancing room.

For grown-ups

Freezing is the hard part, so celebrate magnificent statues loudly. Wobblers sit out one round beside the judge, where the next dance starts.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Give each pause a statue theme — zoo animals, superheroes, robots — so every freeze becomes a tiny invention.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Nature Scavenger Hunt.

A Nature Scavenger Hunt sends spotters outdoors with a short list — a smooth stone, a yellow leaf, something a bird would like — and every find gets checked off and shared.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Make a simple list of safe things to spot.
  2. Explore the area with a grown-up.
  3. Check off each discovery and share what you found.

Skill practiced: Look + Discover — printed on the card.

What you need

A short picture or word list and a pocket or basket for treasures.

For grown-ups

Keep the list to things that are truly findable and truly collectable — spots, leaves and stones, never living things. A grown-up walks along the whole way.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Hunt for sounds as well as sights — a birdsong, footsteps, wind — and end by drawing the best find instead of keeping it.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Obstacle Course.

An Obstacle Course is any safe path you invent: step over cushions, crawl under a chair, hop between spots — then cheer the next player through the same course.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Set up a safe path with simple obstacles.
  2. Move through the course by stepping, crawling, or hopping.
  3. Take turns and cheer for each player.

Skill practiced: Move + Try — printed on the card.

What you need

Household things that climb, duck and balance: cushions, a hoop, a low stool.

For grown-ups

Build it together and test every obstacle yourself first — the rule is one child on the course at a time, and nothing wobbly stays in.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Time nothing and score nothing; instead give each obstacle a story — over the troll bridge, through the bear cave, past the sleepy dragon.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Parachute Pop.

Parachute Pop needs every player gripping the edge: lift the parachute high together, then call one friend to dash underneath before it floats back down.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Everyone holds the edge of a play parachute.
  2. Lift it up together.
  3. Call a player to run underneath, then switch places.

Skill practiced: Lift + Share — printed on the card.

What you need

A play parachute — or a large bedsheet works beautifully.

For grown-ups

Practise the lift first so the fabric rises above heads, not into them, and let the runner choose when to go — the popcorn moment is the thrill.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Bounce a soft ball on top and try not to let it roll off, or make waves — little sea, big sea, storm — with shaking wrists.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Relay Race.

A Relay Race splits players into small teams: run to the marker and back, slap hands with the next runner, and keep the chain going until every teammate has run.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Split into small teams.
  2. Run to the marker and back.
  3. Tag the next player until everyone has a turn.

Skill practiced: Run + Teamwork — printed on the card.

What you need

A marker, teams of any size, and a stretch of safe running ground.

For grown-ups

Run out-and-back courses rather than loops so you can watch every runner, and pair confident runners next to brand-new ones for the cheer.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Swap running for hopping, crab-walking or backwards stepping — or pass a baton, a spoon or a very serious rubber chicken.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Ring Toss.

Ring Toss is a gentle aiming game: toss your three rings one at a time toward the targets, then count together how many landed — and try again to beat it.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Place safe targets a short distance away.
  2. Give each player three soft rings.
  3. Toss gently and count how many rings land on a target.

Skill practiced: Aim + Count — printed on the card.

What you need

Three soft rings and safe targets: cones, bottles or a cardboard tube.

For grown-ups

Start close enough that landing a ring is likely, then step back one heel-to-toe step at a time. Counting the rings is the quiet maths lesson.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Give targets point values and add them up, or toss under a leg, with eyes shut for one giggle throw, or backwards.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Sack Race.

In a Sack Race, each player steps into a sack, holds it at the waist, and hops to the finish line in a series of bouncy jumps — then it is the next racer’s turn.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Give each player a sack.
  2. Step inside and hold the sack at the waist.
  3. Hop to the finish, then take turns cheering for everyone.

Skill practiced: Hop + Laugh — printed on the card.

What you need

One pillowcase or sack per racer and grass or carpet to land on.

For grown-ups

Hop on grass or rugs, never tile, and keep the course short — tired legs and hard floors are the only real danger here. Laughter is guaranteed anyway.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Race in pairs side by side, or make the course turn a corner, or hop to music that everyone must hop in time with.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Shadow Shapes.

Shadow Shapes plays with sunshine: one player strikes a shape — star, bridge, flamingo — and the partner tries to copy the shape exactly, shadows and all, before they swap.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Stand in a safe sunny spot.
  2. Make a shape with your body.
  3. Let a partner copy the shape, then swap roles.

Skill practiced: Pose + Copy — printed on the card.

What you need

A sunny day, a safe patch of light, and bendable bodies.

For grown-ups

Stand where the shadows fall clear and long, and try the shape side by side so both silhouettes show. Cloudy days postpone, never cancel.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Trace each other’s shadow shapes in chalk and colour them in, or make a two-player shape with arms linked into one giant star.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Shape Hunt.

Shape Hunt sends players searching for the world’s hidden geometry: choose three shapes, then find and name safe objects that match — a clock for a circle, a book for a rectangle.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Choose three simple shapes.
  2. Find safe objects with those shapes.
  3. Point, name, and count each one.

Skill practiced: Look + Learn — printed on the card.

What you need

Agreed-on shapes and watchful eyes; paper cutouts make the hunt official.

For grown-ups

Accept careful near-misses with a smile — "that ball is a bit of a circle, isn’t it!" — and count each find out loud together.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Hunt one shape per day, or flip the game: hold up a shape and race to touch something in the room that matches it.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Tag.

Tag is the chase classic: one player is "it", everyone stays inside the play area, and a gentle hand-tag passes the "it" on to a new chaser.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Choose one player to be ‘it’.
  2. Everyone runs within the play area.
  3. The player who is ‘it’ tags someone, who becomes ‘it’ next.

Skill practiced: Run + React — printed on the card.

What you need

An agreed play area with clear edges and shoes that grip.

For grown-ups

Agree the boundaries and the gentle-hand rule before the first chase, and change "it" often so the fastest runner does not keep the title all afternoon.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Play freeze tag — tagged players hold still until a friend unfreezes them — or shadow tag, where stepping on a shadow does the tagging.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Target Toss.

Target Toss aims three soft beanbags at numbered targets: stand back, toss gently, and count how many targets you reached — then hand the beanbags to the next player.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Place safe targets a short distance away.
  2. Give each player three soft beanbags.
  3. Toss gently and count how many targets you reach.

Skill practiced: Aim + Count — printed on the card.

What you need

Three soft beanbags and safe targets — buckets, baskets or taped circles.

For grown-ups

Numbered buckets quietly teach counting and order; start one big step away and move back only when the tosses land. Beanbags, never balls, indoors.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Let each player arrange the targets their own way before their turn — a triangle, a row, a tower of two — and cheer every layout.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Three-Legged Race.

A Three-Legged Race ties partners together: stand side by side, band the inside legs softly, and walk — slowly, in step — all the way to the finish line.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Pair up and stand side by side.
  2. Tie the inside legs together with a soft band.
  3. Walk carefully to the finish, then swap partners.

Skill practiced: Coordinate + Cooperate — printed on the card.

What you need

Soft cloth bands or scarves, pairs of willing partners, and a short grassy course.

For grown-ups

Tie above the knee and never so tight it pinches, and practise the "ready, step" chant — the pairs who count together wobble the least.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Race as a three-legged chain of four, or swap walking for a giant, careful hop on the count of three.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Traffic Cop.

Traffic Cop puts one player in charge of the streets: the rest walk, stop or turn only when the cop’s signal says so — then a new cop takes the whistle.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Choose one player to be the traffic cop.
  2. Walk, stop, or turn when the cop gives a signal.
  3. Change traffic cops so everyone gets a turn.

Skill practiced: Stop + Go — printed on the card.

What you need

Space to walk a pretend street; a toy whistle or a paper flag for authority.

For grown-ups

Teach the two signals first — hand up means stop, hand sweeping means go — and let the smallest cop start with just those two before adding turns.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Add a crossing guard moment — "green for the ducks, red for the cars" — or drive pretend cars and let the cop direct the traffic jam.

KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · ACTIVE PLAY

How to Play Tunnel Crawl.

Tunnel Crawl builds a passage and conquers it: make a safe tunnel from hoops, chairs and cushions, then crawl through one player at a time — and rebuild it a new way each round.

Teaching tips

The card’s three rules

  1. Make a safe tunnel with hoops or soft cushions.
  2. Crawl through the tunnel one at a time.
  3. Take turns building a new path.

Skill practiced: Crawl + Create — printed on the card.

What you need

Cushions, a play tunnel or chair-and-blanket engineering, and knees ready to crawl.

For grown-ups

Steady every tunnel with your hand the first crawl through, and keep one player at each end so the builder never becomes the roof.

Make it fresh tomorrow

Crawl backwards out of the tunnel like a crab, or add a second tunnel and let the players choose their own secret route.
